messages:
sam: Heads-up — we saw a spike where delegation claim batching exploded authz cache invalidations for the operator proxy.  ~100k invalidations in 10m. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: whoa. timeline? is this after the recent batching change in ingress-proxy? :eyes: 

sam: yeah, pushed yesterday. short summary: we batch delegation lookups per upstream request group to reduce RTTs, but we ended up coalescing tokens with slightly different claim sets into the same cache key. When any TTL changes we invalidate widely.

eli: can you paste the header example? trying to picture the merge gate.

sam: sure — current header pattern we use: 

```
Authorization: Delegation token uv1;claims=sub:123,projects:[p1,p2];ttl=600
X-Delegation-Group: g-42
```

sam: batching groups by X-Delegation-Group. problem: claims list ordering and project list normalization differ between services so keys mismatch and we canonicalize incorrectly.

natalie: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) normalize and sort claims/projects before batching keying, 2) only batch tokens that share exact stable-signer id. both cheaper than rolling back.

eli: +1 to normalization. also consider adding a short fingerprint derived from canonical claims instead of inline lists in the key. reduces key size and accidental collisions.

maya: SRE question — what's the expected invalidation window if we normalize? does it reduce invalidations or just change pattern?

sam: rough estimate from replay: normalizing reduces unique keys by ~60% and cuts invalidation events by ~70% in the spike trace. still need guardrails.

ops-bot: incident alert created: INC-2024-2716 — authz-cache-churn. assigned to eng-security oncall.

natalie: another pattern: use two-level cache. level-1 keyed by fingerprint that is cheap and stable; level-2 keyed by full claimset for high-fidelity checks. invalidate L1 only when signer or TTL changes, L2 on claim mutation. tradeoff: extra lookup latency on L1-miss.

eli: can we push an opt-in canary: enable normalization + fingerprinting for 10% of traffic on dedicated route, measure miss rates and latency delta?

sam: yes. I'll open a tiny rollout PR and a dashboard query. plan: do normalization in proxy, add fingerprint header `X-Del-FP`, enable for 10% traffic, watch invalidation_count and p50 authz latency.

maya: ping me on the PR, I'll help wire the dashboard and add an alert threshold (invalidations > 500/min) to auto-rollback.

natalie: also add a metric for cache-hit-by-fp vs cache-hit-by-full-key so we can see mismatch rate.

eli: one more gotcha: canonicalization must be stable across languages — go/python/node services must implement same sort order/normalization rules or the fingerprint lies. add a tiny shared lib or proto doc.

sam: agreed. I'll author a short canonicalization spec in the repo (deterministic sort, normalize project ids to lower-case, remove duplicates) and include unit tests.

maya: ok let's run the canary tomorrow 09:00 PT. good plan. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — filing PR and RFC follow-up note.

natalie: nice work catching this fast.

eli: thanks. keep us posted.
_notes: thread captures an eng-security sync about delegation claim batching, canonicalization, mitigation plans, and canary rollout. messages are short per slack style and include code snippet and bot alert.
